The result is a quietly ironic structure: the phrase “daikichi” is uttered, yet the sensory world the poem actually renders is one of unbroken shadow and moisture. This tension between declared fortune and depicted obscurity produces a restrained but pointed critique of seasonal optimism; renewal is acknowledged only as a rumor glimpsed through conditions that continue to deny it.
